title: content.autoTune
description: Runs AUTO on a content with an explicit mode, key and parameters. It never uses the mode of the AUTO button, the positions of the UI's knobs or the scale shown in the transport bar (PROTOCOL.md section 21 rule 1). mode regenerate regenerates the notes in ranges from the original pitch and snaps them to key, as the AUTO button does in the openTune scheme: the notes inside a range are replaced (removed and created), and notes that touch the edge of a range are dropped instead of regenerated, which the result reports in removed and with the warning DROPPED_BOUNDARY_NOTES (data.notes: [{note, startContentSec, endContentSec}] at the revision before the call). mode snapNotes moves the targets of the existing notes in ranges to key, as the AUTO button does in the openDyne scheme; it takes no params. mode notesOnly generates notes for the whole content and replaces all its notes; as in OpenTune there is no undo entry, and the previous notes cannot be restored (warnings REPLACES_ALL_NOTES, data {removedCount, createdCount}, and IRREVERSIBLE). mode reference aligns the pitch of the placement placementId to the clip it has a reference binding to, as the AUTO button does for such a clip: it needs the capability reference.v1 besides edit.v1 (x-otcp.valueCapabilities; else UNSUPPORTED(capability_missing)), a placementId that shows the content contentId names (else INVALID_ARGUMENT(placement_content_mismatch)) and a reference binding on that placement (else INVALID_ARGUMENT(reference_not_bound)), and takes no ranges, key, params or dryRun. It runs as a job of kind referenceAnalysis: when the binding has no alignment data yet (content.getDetails, reference.alignmentReady false), the job first computes it, as content.analyzeReference does, and then aligns the whole content in one undo step; the job's result (jobResult) is the write envelope with the members of result, keyUsed and paramsUsed null. A reference binding stays on a clip until it is removed (arrangement.edit, op setReference with null), and while it is there OpenTune's AUTO button runs reference alignment instead of the mode of the editing scheme (content.getDetails, autoModes.uiButtonRuns reference). content.autoTune never infers its mode, so regenerate, snapNotes and notesOnly ignore a binding, and only mode reference uses it. ranges (content clock, at most 16) default to the whole content; one call is one undo step. key is an explicit key or clipKey, the content's own key, which then needs expectedKeyRevision (REVISION_CONFLICT(key_changed)). Absent params members take the note generator's defaults, not the UI's knob positions; paramsUsed and keyUsed report what was used. changes, created and removed list at most 200 entries each and omittedCount counts the rest; content.getNotes reads them at the new revision.

keyUsed.description: The key the notes were snapped to; null for notesOnly and reference, and in a result that hands the work to a job (the job's result reports it).

paramsUsed.description: The generator parameters used; null for snapNotes, and in a result that hands the work to a job.

noteCount.description: Notes of the content before and after the work; null in a result that hands the work to a job.

jobResult.description: The result of the referenceAnalysis job: the write envelope of the committed work, with the members of result.
